EXPLANATION: The most intense low-frequency band is at 667 cm⁻¹, the typical region for a C–Cl stretch (rule GFQ-046).  Among the ten candidates only molecule 1 (ClCC1COCO1) contains a Cl atom, making it uniquely compatible with this strong feature.  The series of medium-strong peaks at 750, 808, 838 and 889 cm⁻¹ match ring-breathing and C–O–C vibrations expected for a 1,3-dioxolane ring, which is present in candidate 1.  CH stretching bands at 2879, 2965 and 3014 cm⁻¹ and the CH₂ scissoring band at 1458 cm⁻¹ are consistent with the aliphatic groups in this molecule.  No other candidate simultaneously provides a C–Cl bond and a 1,3-dioxolane skeleton, so candidate 1 best explains the observed Raman spectrum.
